text:
Nazem Kadri is back in Colorado, 34 games into a second stint with the team he won the 2022 Stanley Cup with, and at 36 he has found his scoring again. All five of his goals have come in his last ten games. The Nov. 2 game in Chicago showed both sides of him: the Denver Gazette's Evan Rawal flagged his turnover that set up a 2-0 Blackhawks lead, and then Kadri scored twice in a 5-2 comeback that Reuters credited to him and Jaden Schwartz.

The underlying numbers are steady rather than spectacular. He has 14 points in 18 games on 6.1 expected goals, and his 10.9% shooting sits right in his talent range. Colorado's 5v5 share with him is just under 52%, a touch below its share without him, and his ice time over the last ten games is about 17.4 minutes.

What he still does well is draw penalties: Evolving-Hockey valued that at 2.6 goals last season, most of his value. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking also had him in the 88th percentile for primary shot assists. Our projection: 55 points.
headline: Kadri's second Colorado act finds its scoring touch
